name: GSLV Mk II (S139+4 L40H+GL40HT+CUS15)

propellant_kg.derived: F18 brochure 4 L40H load 170.6 t /4 = 42,650 kg, minus 1331 kg burned on the pad (strap-ons ignite T-4.8 s per GSLV-F15 sequence https://www.isro.gov.in/media_isro/pdf/GSLVF15/GSLV-F15_NVS-02_EngBrochure240125.pdf) at the derived mdot

dry_kg.derived: (stage mass at lift-off 191 t - propellant 170.6 t)/4, F18 brochure https://www.isro.gov.in/media_isro/image/index/GSLVF18_NVS03/GSLV_F18_NVS03_Mission_Brouchure_27102026.pdf

thrust_vac_N.derived: mdot 277.3 kg/s (= 42,650 kg / 153.8 s burn, T-4.8 s to published shut-off T+149 s) x Isp_vac 293 s x g0; Vikas Isp https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vikas_(rocket_engine)

thrust_sl_N.derived: same mdot x Isp_SL 262 s x g0 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vikas_(rocket_engine)); Wikipedia lists 760 kN per L40H (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geosynchronous_Satellite_Launch_Vehicle)

ignition_s.derived: lifts off at S139 ignition T0 (strap-ons ignite at T-4.8 s; pad burn removed from load)

cutoff_s.note: GSLV-F15 published '4L40H shut off 149 s' (F18 sequence unpublished; F15 = same vehicle, same NVS GTO mission class)

separation_s.note: GS1/GS2 separation 151.2 s (strap-ons leave with GS1)

dry_kg.derived: stage mass at lift-off 160.9 t - propellant 138.2 t, F18 brochure https://www.isro.gov.in/media_isro/image/index/GSLVF18_NVS03/GSLV_F18_NVS03_Mission_Brouchure_27102026.pdf

thrust_vac_N.derived: average mdot 1,382 kg/s (= 138.2 t / 100 s nominal burn, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geosynchronous_Satellite_Launch_Vehicle) x Isp_vac 269 s (PSLV PS1 S139, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PSLV) x g0; Wikipedia peak thrust 4,846.9 kN

thrust_sl_N.derived: same mdot x Isp_SL 237 s (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geosynchronous_Satellite_Launch_Vehicle) x g0

cutoff_s.assumption: S139 nominal burn time 100 s (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geosynchronous_Satellite_Launch_Vehicle); not in the F15/F18 event tables; constant mdot (real solid thrust is regressive)

dry_kg.derived: stage mass 47.3 t - propellant 42.1 t, F18 brochure https://www.isro.gov.in/media_isro/image/index/GSLVF18_NVS03/GSLV_F18_NVS03_Mission_Brouchure_27102026.pdf

thrust_vac_N.derived: full-depletion mdot 297.40 kg/s (= F18 load 42.1 t / F15 published burn 149.6->291.16 s) x Isp 295 s x g0; Wikipedia lists 846.8 kN (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geosynchronous_Satellite_Launch_Vehicle), +1.6%

dry_kg.derived: stage mass 17.1 t - propellant 14.4 t, F18 brochure https://www.isro.gov.in/media_isro/image/index/GSLVF18_NVS03/GSLV_F18_NVS03_Mission_Brouchure_27102026.pdf

thrust_vac_N.derived: full-depletion mdot 17.149 kg/s (= F18 load 14.4 t / F15 published burn 295.68->1135.38 s; F15 'CUS burn out' follows shut-off by 5 s) x Isp 454 s x g0; published CE-7.5 73.5 kN (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CE-7.5) / 75 kN (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geosynchronous_Satellite_Launch_Vehicle)

cutoff_s.note: CUS shut off 1135.38 s (CUS burn out 1140.38 s, S/C separation 1150.38 s)

mass_kg.derived: budget: F18 '~420 t' lift-off mass - stage masses (160.9+191+47.3+17.1 t) - payload 2.25 t = 1.45 t for 3.4 m metallic PLF + adapter (rough: lift-off mass is rounded)

cd.basis: ASSUMPTION bound for slender LV mean Cd (reference area = 2.8 m core; 3.4 m PLF absorbed into Cd)

header_notes: GSLV Mk II TIMELINE mode: stage/fairing event times are ISRO's PUBLISHED GSLV-F15/NVS-02 sequence (same vehicle, same 2,250 kg NVS GTO class); ISRO has not published an F18 event table.
Stage loads and masses from the ISRO GSLV-F18/NVS-03 brochure (27 Oct 2026); thrust/Isp from Wikipedia (GSLV, Vikas, CE-7.5, PSLV) with derivations noted.
